Q: ERROR in app: Exception on /_dash-update-component [POST] A:

Custom INFO log message suppression

NOTE:
Seeing that all AI and google redirects to this question, I will provide the answer on how to suppress this specific message.

If you came here from some search engine, after having searched for how to suppress this message from a python Dash/Flash server, then do the following.

This will suppress only this message:

127.0.0.1 - - [19/Jul/2026 04:58:23] "POST /_dash-update-component HTTP/1.1" 200 -

The code:

import logging

# Set custom logger to filter Dash/Flask (web update) spam:

class Suppress200Filter(logging.Filter):
    def filter(self, record):
        message = record.getMessage()
        # Suppress only the "_dash-update-component" with 200 status
        if "_dash-update-component" in message and " 200 " in message:
            return False
        return True

def SetupCustomLogger():
    # Set log level [4]:
    # [NOTSET,DEBUG,INFO,WARNING,ERROR,CRITICAL] = 0,10,20,30,40,50
    log = logging.getLogger('werkzeug')
    log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    log.addFilter(Suppress200Filter())

...
SetupCustomLogger()
...

Q: Where is the C Standard function sqrt actually defined? (Windows user) A:

Where is the C Standard function sqrt actually defined?

The C23 spec has 7.12.7.10 The sqrt functions

double sqrt(double x);

The sqrt functions compute the nonnegative square root of x. A domain error occurs if the argument is less than zero.
The sqrt functions return √ x.

about how it is defined inside the C Standard Library and my machine.

An implementation may use additional keywords. C does not, itself specify how or even how well the square root is implemented.

Even if today, one reviews the source code of an implementation, a subsequent version is not obligate to perform like a pervious one.

Yet sqrt(x) is a very well understood function. A quality sqrt() is readily achievable and expected in 2026. So good the result is expected to be the best result.

Of note, an implementation that follows IEEE 754, sqrt(-0.0) is -0.0 which somewhat goes against compute the nonnegative square root of x.

Q: Adding HTTP security headers to WSO2 APIM (4.1.0) /service and /services endpoints A:

Building on the existing answers, if your goal is simply to stop /service and /services from being publicly reachable at all — rather than adding headers to them — there's a simpler option than a custom Tomcat filter or Axis2 handler: disable the endpoint directly via configuration.

In <APIM_HOME>/repository/conf/deployment.toml, add:

toml

[transport.http]
disable_wsdl_endpoint = true

Restart the server. Both /services and its WSDL listing will stop responding externally with a single config change — no custom Java filter or XML handler required.

This aligns with the general security guidance already given here: these are internal Axis2/SOAP admin endpoints, not part of your public API surface, so the safest default is usually to disable them rather than try to secure them in place.

When this won't work: if you actually need /services reachable (some internal tooling depends on it) but still want the security headers attached, this config flag won't help — headers still need to be injected via the Tomcat HttpHeaderSecurityFilter approach in the answer above, since this endpoint doesn't pass through Synapse mediation and deployment.toml alone can't inject response headers into it.

I haven't tested disable_wsdl_endpoint specifically against 4.1.0, so worth confirming it's still the same key in your version before relying on it in production.

Q: Django Deployment - scriptProcessor could not be found in fastCGI application configuration A:

To resolve the issue, I encountered, I copied the fullPath and arguments values from the applicationHost.config file, specifically within the fastCgi tag, and then pasted them into the web.config file of my application. Additionally, I made sure to update the

<section name="handlers" overrideModeDefault="Allow" />

line in the applicationHost.config file.
